title: Dates past 9999 and before year 1: computed, up to DuckDB's own limits
verdict: computes past 0001-01-01 … 9999-12-31; the written plan guards
description: Date arithmetic is not limited to 0001-01-01 … 9999-12-31: `DATE '9999-12-31' + 1` is `10000-01-01`, `DATE '0001-01-01' - 1` is `0001-12-31 (BC)` (year 0), and an interval of months or a second past a timestamp's last one carry on. `year(DATE '0001-01-01' - 1)` is 0.

DuckDB's dates run from 5877642-06-25 BC to 5881580-07-10; a day past either raises `Out of Range Error: Date out of range`. `DATE + INTERVAL` gives a timestamp, whose range is narrower (to 294247-01-10): past it, `Conversion Error: Date and time not in timestamp range`.
reference: `date_range`: date arithmetic whose operand or result leaves 0001-01-01 … 9999-12-31 raises (#251), reported by `verify`. The written SQL checks the result against the reference's dates and raises "outside the reference's dates" (`sql/core/_base.py`), so DuckDB's wider range is never returned; with constant operands the check is made when the plan is written.
